# Writing a `redirect` page

Generated from `redirect`'s own template declarations. It states what this type requires;
the rules that apply to every page are in `wiki-authoring-spec.md` beside this file.

- **Authorship** `derived` — an agent authors it from named `sources:`
- **Freshness** stale after never

## Frontmatter

Required on this type beyond the base fields (`title`, `type`, `created`, `updated`, `owner`, `authorship`):

- `target`
- `archived`
- `reason`

The template also scaffolds `sources`, `related` — fill or empty each one; leaving a placeholder is an error.

## Placeholders to replace

{{TITLE}} {{PATH}} {{ARCHIVED}} {{REASON}} {{DATE}} {{OWNER}}. {{PATH}} is the original page path without prefix or extension — the frontmatter target takes the slash form, the body link the colon form. Leaving one in place is an error (`unsubstituted-token`), and so is leaving a template example line (`template-example-line`).

Run `/wiki-conformance-audit` for the checks that apply and the verdict.

## After you save

Two steps finish the page and neither is in the template:

- Commit the file under your own identity — authorship is a git fact, not a frontmatter one.
- Run `/wiki-reindex` so the page appears in its sub-wiki `index.md` and in `_derived/cited-by.md`. Until then it exists but nothing links to it.
